children: By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
An MSCI index of emerging market stocks fell on Tuesday in the lead-up to earnings from chip heavyweight Nvidia, while fresh US curbs on AI chip exports to China kept investors cautious.

The US administration tightened restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips, raising concerns about a fragile trade truce between Washington and Beijing ahead of US President Donald Trump's talks with China's President Xi Jinping.
Meanwhile, anticipation was building for Nvidia's
earnings, with markets assessing whether strong demand for AI infrastructure can be sustained, while also weighing the implications of CEO Jensen Huang's departure.
"Nvidia’s results are always a key test for the AI trade, but even more so in the current environment," said Francesco Pesole, FX strategist at ING.
MSCI's emerging market equities index
CBOE:EFS
slipped 1.3%, while the corresponding currencies gauge (.MIEM00000CUS) was flat as the US dollar strengthened.
A broader selloff in global equities supported the dollar's safe-haven appeal, offsetting the impact of expectations for a less aggressive Federal Reserve, Pesole said.
In central Europe, currencies edged lower as investors awaited a Hungarian central bank rate decision, while a firmer dollar also weighed on regional sentiment.
Hungarian equities were weaker, with the Budapest benchmark falling 0.7%, pressured by banking stocks such as Granit Bank
and OTP Bank
, which fell more than 1% each.
Emerging market sovereign bond spreads remained elevated, reflecting lingering caution towards riskier debt.
OIL GAINS; BROKERAGE UPGRADES UAE, TURKEY
Oil prices rose as concerns over a potential supply disruption intensified after Iran's military said an oil tanker was heavily damaged by a mine in the Strait of Hormuz.

Separately, JPMorgan upgraded the UAE to "overweight", citing the Gulf state's economic resilience despite months of regional conflict and saying it expected the country's stock market to outperform broader CEEMEA markets.

The brokerage also upgraded Turkey to "overweight" from "neutral", saying the investment fund crisis that rattled the country's financial markets had largely run its course and that equities were poised for a rebound.
M‌eanwhile, South Korea
hit its lowest close since early February, while Taiwan stocks
TWSE:TAIEX
clocked their worst two-day decline since July, down more than 7% so far this week.
The Taiwan Stock Exchange will take necessary stabilisation measures to maintain orderly trading if there are irrational, sustained declines or abnormal volatility, it said late on Monday.
Ukraine's dollar-denominated bonds were slightly lower.

Ukraine struck the strategically important bridge linking southern Russia and Crimea for the second time in two days, the Black Sea peninsula's Russian-backed governor said on Tuesday, part of what was the biggest Ukrainian drone attack of the war, according to the defence ministry.
